Dataset title: Quarterly Financial Report (QFR)
Description: The Quarterly Financial Report (QFR) program collects and publishes quarterly aggregate statistics on the financial results and position of U.S. corporations. The program currently collects and publishes financial data for the manufacturing, mining, wholesale trade, retail trade, information, and professional and technical services (except legal) sectors. The survey is a principal economic indicator that provides financial data essential to calculation of key U.S. government measures of national economic performance. prompts.assessment:
# Dataset risk assessment
I would like your help in assessing the likelihood that this data will be changed or removed from its primary location, and that users will no longer be able to access accurate and reliable copies of it, based on the rubric below.

## Sources for context
To help assess the rubric categories, perform additional research on the data, the agency, the data's topics and typical users, covering topics such as proposed regulatory or funding changes, recent news, and political commentary. Use whatever resources you find useful, including the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov) and the federal staffing tracker at https://usajobs-tracker.abigailhaddad.com.

## Rubric
This rubric is divided up into categories. Each category is divided up into risk levels. In your output, please select the appropriate risk level for each category based on your research.

### Historical Data Availability
- Gone: Data files prior to the current year or cycle are no longer publicly available.
- High Risk: Some data files prior to the current year or cycle are removed.
- Moderate Risk: Some data elements that exist in the dataset prior to the current year or cycle are removed.
- No Known Issue: Data prior to the current year or cycle remain accessible with no known alterations.

### Future Data Availability
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Statutory publication deadline missed and/or collection or publication skipped and/or ICR expired for more than one year.
- Moderate Risk: Typical or intended publication date missed and/or collection or publication delayed; ICR expired up to one year.
- No Known Issue: Data published on time or as expected and ICR active or renewed before expiration.

### Data Quality
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Reductions in granularity, timeliness, or frequency.
- Moderate Risk: Potential or emerging risk to granularity, timeliness, or frequency.
- No Known Issue: Maintained or improved granularity, timeliness, or frequency.

### Statutory Context
- Gone: N/A
- High Risk: Statutory authorization is vague and/or there are alternative data collections that could serve as substitutes and/or no known programmatic use.
- Moderate Risk: Not explicitly required by statute but required for the implementation of a state or federal program, and there are no alternative data collections that could serve as substitutes.
- No Known Issue: Statutorily required and/or statutory authorization is explicitly named and it is clear what has to be collected, and there aren't alternative data collections that could serve as substitutes and/or required for implementation of a federal program.

### Staffing and Funding
- Gone: All of the staff in the division or agency are gone and/or all funding has been terminated.
- High Risk: 40% or more of staff lost, and/or 1,000 or more staff lost, and/or budget cut by 20% or more, and/or leadership removed.
- Moderate Risk: 10–39% of staff lost, and/or 500–999 staff lost, and/or budget cut by 10–19%, and/or threatened change in leadership.
- No Known Issue: Less than 10% of staff lost and less than 10% of budget cut and no known change in leadership.

### Policy
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Presidential Action-driven information collection request (ICR); negative policy note on site; other significant changes in accordance with Administration priorities.
- Moderate Risk: Proposed or pending changes; statements by administration officials suggesting a change is being considered or planned.
- No Known Issue: No notable changes since January 2025 affecting what data is collected and published.

For each category, concisely list the evidence and supporting sources that would support each risk level. Then indicate which risk level you find most appropriate and why.

Conclude with a simple summary of risk levels:
Historical Data Availability: <level>
Future Data Availability: <level>
Data Quality: <level>
Statutory Context: <level>
Staffing and Funding: <level>
Policy: <level>

Quarterly Financial Report (QFR)
Manufacturing, Mining, Trade, and Selected Service Industries

Purpose

  • For over sixty years, the QFR program has collected and published quarterly aggregate statistics on the financial results and position of U.S. corporations.

History

  • The program's origin dates back to World War II, when the responsibility for collecting data relating to economic activity
    in the U.S. was in the hands of the Office of Price Administration (OPA).
  • At the conclusion of the war, the program was transferred to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
    and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which jointly administered the program.
  • In 1971, the FTC took over sole responsibility for administering the QFR program.
  • The QFR program was transferred to the U.S. Census Bureau in 1982.
  • The QFR converted from SIC to NAICS in Fourth Quarter 2001, restating Fourth Quarter 2000 to First Quarter 2001 in NAICS.
  • In Fourth Quarter 2010, Fourth Quarter 2009 to Third Quarter 2010 was restated to reflect the implementation of an improved imputation methodology.
  • The QFR program expanded to include Selected Service Industries 511-512, 515, 517-519, 541 (except 5411 Legal Services) in Fourth Quarter 2010.
  • The QFR program began seasonally adjusting Retail Sales in Second Quarter 2012.
  • The QFR program began releasing Retail together with Manufacturing, Mining, Wholesale, and Selected Service Industries in First Quarter 2016.

Coverage

  • Corporations that have a plurality of business activity in manufacturing industries, and domestic assets of $250,000 and over.
  • Corporations that have a plurality of business activity in mining, wholesale trade, retail trade, or selected service industries, and domestic assets of $50 million and over.
  • Corporations that are above industry specific receipt cut-off values.
  • The statistical data are classified by industry and by asset size.
  • Currently, the QFR program covers the following industry sectors, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS):
     
    • Mining                                      211-213
    • Manufacturing                           311-316, 321-327, 331-337, 339
    • Wholesale Trade                       423-425
    • Retail Trade                              441-448, 451-454
    • Selected Service Industries         511-512, 515, 517-519, 541 (except 5411 Legal Services)

Content

  • Based upon a sample survey, the QFR presents estimated statements of income and retained earnings, balance sheets, and related financial and operating ratios.

Legal Authority and Confidentiality

YOUR RESPONSE IS REQUIRED BY LAW. Title 13 of the United States Code, Section 91, authorizes this collection and requires that financial statistics of business operations be collected and published quarterly.

Title 13, United States Code, Section 9, requires the Census Bureau to keep your information CONFIDENTIAL and to use your responses only to produce statistics.

The Census Bureau is not permitted to publicly release your responses in a way that could identify your business, organization or institution.

Per the Federal Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2015, your data are protected from cybersecurity risks through screening of the systems that transmit your data.

Frequency

  • The QFR survey is conducted quarterly.
  • Corporations report for each of their fiscal quarters, and are included in published calendar quarter estimates depending on the month their books are closed.
  • QFR data are released for the calendar quarter approximately 75 days after the end of the first, second, and third calendar quarters,
    and approximately 90 days after the end of the fourth calendar quarter.
  • The extended fourth quarter is to accommodate annual reporting obligations and include holiday sales.
  • The following table displays the four reporting quarters by industry sector in terms of the month in which any selected corporation's fiscal quarter ends:
QFR Quarter Manufacturing, Mining, Wholesale Trade, and Selected Service Industries Retail Trade
First January, February, or March February, March, or April
Second April, May, or June May, June, or July
Third July, August, or September August, September, or October
Fourth October, November, or December November, December, or January


Methods

  • QFR utilizes a mail-out/mail-back survey.
  • Approximately 4,600 large corporations in manufacturing, mining, trade, and selected service industries are mailed a long form.
  • Approximately 5,000 selected small- and medium-sized manufacturing corporations are mailed a short form.
  • The sample frame of firms is updated annually from Federal income tax records.
  • Using the tax data, corporations are selected by stratified random sample, with strata by industry and asset size.
  • Data for manufacturing corporations with assets between $250,000 and $250 million are estimated from a sample panel.
  • Each quarter, one-eighth of the sample panel is replaced. Corporations selected in the sample report for 8 quarters.

Products

  • A press release is issued concurrent with each QFR data release, summarizing the results contained within the publication.
  • Press releases are issued in both PDF and Excel formats, and are available on this web site in Historical Data.
  • Each QFR publication includes information on the most recently closed quarters for manufacturing, mining, wholesale trade, and selected service industries, and retail trade.
  • Information on the most recently closed quarters for retail trade are available in the quarterly press releases, and in the fourth quarter QFR publication,
    where the 90-day schedule permits synchronized presentation.
  • Publications are issued in both PDF and Excel formats, and are available on this web site in Historical Data.
  • Historical QFR data are available in Excel format on this web site in Historical Data.

Uses of the Data

  • The QFR data are a primary source for current estimates of corporate profits for the Nation's Gross Domestic Income Accounts.
  • QFR data are widely used by government agencies, domestic and foreign businesses, financial analysts, researchers, trade associations, and banking institutions.
  • Uses include assessing industrial debt structure, liquidity, and profitability; estimating corporate tax liability; designing economic policies and drafting legislation;
    making investment evaluations; and studying economic trends.

RELATED PRODUCTS

Business Expenses Supplement (formerly Business Expenses Survey)

Annual Survey of Manufactures

Monthly M3 Survey

Annual Retail Trade Survey

Monthly Retail Trade Survey

Annual Trade Survey

Monthly Wholesale Trade Survey

Annual Capital Expenditures Survey

Investment Plans Survey (discontinued 1996; formerly the Plant and Equipment Survey)

Economic Census

EXPLORE INFORMATION

CONTINUE OVERVIEW

#data research
I am researching a federal dataset. Find out everything you can about this dataset, such as who publishes it, under what authority or mandate, its history, its typical users, and its benefits to the public. Be sure your research comprehensively covers each of those perspectives, as well as any others that you discover or seem useful. I believe this is accurate information, but please check:

Dataset title: Quarterly Financial Report (QFR)
Description: The Quarterly Financial Report (QFR) program collects and publishes quarterly aggregate statistics on the financial results and position of U.S. corporations. The program currently collects and publishes financial data for the manufacturing, mining, wholesale trade, retail trade, information, and professional and technical services (except legal) sectors. The survey is a principal economic indicator that provides financial data essential to calculation of key U.S. government measures of national economic performance. Several U.S. Census Bureau reports, including Corporate Profits, Retail Trade, and Manufacturing, Mining, and Wholesale Trade, are produced using these data.

Return a complete report on everything that a preservationist, data librarian, data scientist, or policy activist might want to know about this data.

I'll research the Quarterly Financial Report (QFR) program comprehensively. Let me start with several searches covering different angles.I have a strong foundation. Let me dig deeper into data access, users, methodology, and history.Let me check the current ICR details, recent threats/funding issues, and any news relevant to preservationists.I have a search limit reached, so let me fetch the key Census pages directly to complete the picture.I now have comprehensive coverage from primary sources. Here is the complete report.

---

# The Quarterly Financial Report (QFR): A Comprehensive Research Report

## 1. Executive Summary

The Quarterly Financial Report (QFR) is a **principal federal economic indicator** conducted by the **U.S. Census Bureau** (an agency of the Department of Commerce) that has published aggregate quarterly statistics on the financial results and position of U.S. corporations since **1947** — nearly 80 years of continuous data. Based on a mandatory, stratified sample survey of roughly 8,000–10,000 corporations per quarter, it produces estimated income statements, balance sheets, and financial/operating ratios for manufacturing, mining, wholesale trade, retail trade, information, and professional, scientific, and technical services (except legal services) corporations. Its most consequential downstream use is as the **primary source data for the Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly estimates of corporate profits** in GDP/Gross Domestic Income, and as an input to the Federal Reserve's Financial Accounts (Z.1).

**Bottom line for the user's prompt:** The description you provided is substantially accurate, with two refinements noted in Section 8 below (the official sector name is "professional, *scientific*, and technical services (except legal)," and the reports named are QFR's *own* release products rather than other Census programs).

---

## 2. Publisher and Program Administration

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Publisher** | U.S. Census Bureau, Department of Commerce |
| **Program office** | Administered by the Secretary of Commerce under 13 U.S.C. § 91; survey operations run by Census's economic indicator directorates (the current press release carries a "Sample Design Management Branch" imprint) |
| **Program type** | One of the Census Bureau's principal federal economic indicators (alongside e.g., monthly retail trade, construction spending, international trade) |
| **Frequency** | Quarterly; data released ~75 days after Q1–Q3 calendar quarters and ~90–95 days after Q4 (the Q4 extension accommodates annual reporting and holiday retail sales) |
| **Geography** | **National only** — no state, metro, or county detail |
| **Vintage** | Continuous series since 1947 |

---

## 3. Legal Authority and Mandate

The QFR has an unusually specific and traceable statutory pedigree — a point of particular interest to policy researchers:

- **Core authority: 13 U.S.C. § 91** — "The Secretary shall collect and publish quarterly financial statistics of business operations, organization, practices, management, and relation to other businesses, including data on sales, expenses, profits, assets, liabilities, stockholders' equity..." The statute deliberately preserved continuity with the FTC-era program ("shall conform to the quarterly financial reporting program carried out by the Federal Trade Commission before the effective date of this section under section 6(b) of the Federal Trade Commission Act").
- **Enacted by Public Law 97-454 (Jan. 12, 1983)**, which transferred the program (personnel, property, and records) from the Federal Trade Commission to the Secretary of Commerce, effective within 90 days.
- **Sunset/reauthorization structure:** Unlike most Census programs, the QFR authorization carries an expiration date that Congress has repeatedly extended — via P.L. 101-227 (1989), P.L. 103-105 (1993), P.L. 105-252 (1998), P.L. 109-79 (2005), and most recently **P.L. 114-72 (Oct. 22, 2015), the Quarterly Financial Report Reauthorization Act, which extended authority through September 30, 2030** (H.R. 3116, 114th Congress). This is a live policy lever: the program's legal authority will lapse absent another reauthorization before the 2030 date.
- **Mandatory response:** The survey is mandatory under **13 U.S.C. § 91 and § 224** ("Your response is required by law"). This matters analytically — unlike voluntary surveys, nonresponse bias is mitigated by legal compulsion.
- **Confidentiality:** **13 U.S.C. § 9** protects individual responses; data may be used only to produce statistics, may not identify individual businesses, and individual questionnaires cannot be used for taxation, investigation, or regulation.
- **IRS data pipeline:** Section 91(c) and P.L. 97-454 § 2(b) treat the program as a "related statistical activity" under **IRC § 6103(j)(1)**, allowing the Census Bureau to receive corporate tax-return information (Form 1120) to build its sampling frame.
- **Paperwork Reduction Act:** Cleared under **OMB Control No. 0607-0432**; current ICR (202406-0607-001) approved August 15, 2024, expiring August 31, 2027.

---

## 4. History and Program Evolution

The QFR's lineage is one of the longest of any federal economic statistic:

1. **World War II (1940s):** Originated with the **Office of Price Administration (OPA)**, which collected economic activity data for wartime price control.
2. **Postwar:** Transferred to the **Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)**, which jointly administered it.
3. **1971:** FTC took sole responsibility (under FTC Act § 6(b)).
4. **January 1983:** Transferred to the **U.S. Census Bureau** via P.L. 97-454, where it has remained since. (Census materials say "transferred in 1982"; the statute was signed Jan. 12, 1983, with transfer completed within 90 days — the discrepancy reflects the legislative process that began in 1982.)
5. **Q4 2001:** Converted from the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) to **NAICS**, restating Q4 2000–Q1 2001.
6. **Q4 2010:** Two milestones — an improved **imputation methodology** (Q4 2009–Q3 2010 restated) and **expansion to selected service industries** (NAICS 511-512, 515, 517-519, and 541 except legal services — reconstituted after NAICS 2017/2022 revisions as Information 512-513, 516-519 and Professional/Scientific/Technical Services 541 excl. 5411).
7. **Q2 2012:** Began seasonally adjusting retail sales.
8. **Q1 2016:** Retail trade synchronized with the other sectors in the same quarterly release (previously on a one-quarter lag except in Q4).
9. **Q4 2024:** Implemented the **2022 NAICS** revision; estimates from Q4 2024 forward reflect 2022 NAICS, earlier estimates reflect 2017 NAICS — a known series-break for time-series work.

**Data availability by era:** historical *publications* (PDF) from 1996–present; Excel publication tables from 2006–present (retail financial tables 2009–2015); and historical **database tables from 1947–present**.

---

## 5. Coverage, Content, and Methodology

### Population and sector coverage
- **Manufacturing corporations** with domestic assets of roughly $250,000 and over (the current methodology document describes the target population as manufacturing with total assets of $5 million+ for sampling purposes, with asset-size tabulation below that; historical descriptions used $250K).
- Corporations in **mining, wholesale trade, retail trade, information, and professional/scientific/technical services (except legal)** with domestic assets of **$50 million+** or above industry-specific receipt cutoffs.
- Current NAICS coverage: Mining 211–213; Manufacturing 311–316, 321–327, 331–337, 339; Wholesale Trade 423–425; Retail Trade 441–448, 451–454 (also listed as 441, 444–445, 449, 455–459 under 2022 NAICS); Selected Services 512–513, 516–519, 541 (excl. 5411).
- **Not covered:** legal services, finance and insurance, most other service sectors, utilities, construction, transportation, unincorporated businesses. Roughly one-third of corporate profits historically.

### Data collected
Estimated **statements of income and retained earnings, balance sheets, and related financial and operating ratios** — sales, expenses, profits (before and after tax), assets, liabilities, stockholders' equity — classified by industry and asset size. Estimates are published for about **36 types of business activity**.

### Sample design (relevant to data scientists)
- **Frame:** Annual file from the **IRS** of Form 1120 filers; stratified by NAICS industry, total assets, and receipts.
- **Certainty cases:** Corporations with assets ≥ $250 million may be included with certainty and canvassed every quarter until out of scope.
- **Panel rotation:** Non-certainty corporations are sampled by stratified random selection; **one-eighth of the panel is replaced each quarter and firms report for 8 consecutive quarters** (a rotating panel design that balances respondent burden against time-series continuity).
- **Forms:** QFR-200(MT) long form for ~4,300 large corporations (~3.0 hrs/response); QFR-201(MG) for ~2,750 corporations (~1.2 hrs); QFR-300(S) short form for ~1,500 small/medium manufacturing firms (~3.0 hrs). ~4,600 large firms plus ~5,000 small/medium manufacturing firms are canvassed per quarter.
- **Collection mode:** Mail-out/mail-back plus electronic reporting; firms report on their own fiscal quarters and are assigned to calendar quarters based on the month their books close.
- **Quality treatment:** Sampling error is published as ± ranges in press releases (e.g., "±1.2 billion"); documentation covers coverage, collection, response, nonresponse, and processing error; seasonal adjustment measures updated annually in Q2; the 2010 imputation-methodology improvement was retrospectively applied.

### Respondent burden
Per the 2024 ICR: **34,288 responses and 82,898 burden hours annually** (down from 35,148 responses / 84,686 hours in the prior clearance); zero estimated indirect cost burden. OMB's Terms of Clearance require Census to keep reporting on efforts to raise response rates, including size-category comparisons — evidence that nonresponse has been a program concern.

---

## 6. Typical Users and Downstream Dependencies

This is where the QFR's public value is most visible, and where activists would focus:

- **Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA):** The QFR is the **primary source for current (quarterly) estimates of corporate profits, taxes, and dividends** in the National Income and Product Accounts. Per BEA's NIPA Handbook (Ch. 13), QFR "income before taxes" — adjusted for dividend income, nonrecurring items, and foreign operations — is the **indicator series for extrapolating profits in mining, manufacturing, wholesale trade, retail trade, information, and professional/scientific/technical services**. Roughly 75 industries' quarterly profit estimates depend on QFR or a companion source.
- **Federal Reserve Board:** Source data for the **nonfinancial corporate business** sector of the Z.1 Financial Accounts of the United States; also used to assess industrial debt structure, liquidity, and profitability.
- **Treasury Department:** Estimates of **corporate tax liability** for revenue forecasting.
- **Council of Economic Advisers and congressional committees:** key indicators for designing economic policy and drafting legislation.
- **FTC:** reference point for analyzing the financial performance of American industries (a residual role from its former administration of the program).
- **Private sector:** banks, financial analysts, investment managers, trade associations, domestic and foreign businesses, and academic researchers use QFR data for profitability and leverage benchmarks, industry financial-ratio comparisons, investment evaluation, and trend analysis.

---

## 7. Data Access, Products, and Preservation Notes

For data librarians and preservationists:

- **Program homepage:** census.gov/econ/qfr/ — with About, Data (historical), Technical Documentation, Release Schedule, Definitions, and Respondents pages.
- **Historical data** (census.gov/econ/qfr/historic.html):
  - Historical QFR publications in PDF, 1996–present (titled "Manufacturing, Mining, Trade, and Selected Service Industries").
  - Excel publication financial and summary tables, 2006–present; retail financial tables 2009–2015.
  - **Historical QFR database tables, 1947–present** — the deepest time series available.
- **Interactive time series / trend charts:** census.gov/econ/currentdata and /econ_timeseries (programCode=QFR), with bulk Excel download of the entire series.
- **API:** Available through the Census Data API at `api.census.gov/data/timeseries/eits/qfr` (Economic Indicators Time Series; requires a free API key). Variables include data_type_code, time_slot_id, seasonally_adj, category_code, cell_value, and error_data; U.S.-level only.
- **Press releases:** issued with each quarterly release in PDF and Excel.
- **Known breaks/continuity hazards:** SIC→NAICS (2001); services expansion and imputation restatement (2010); 2017→2022 NAICS implementation (Q4 2024); rotating panel design; periodic restatements. Time-series analysis should consult the QFR Methodology PDF (census.gov/econ/qfr/documents/QFR_Methodology.pdf) and the seasonal measures files.
- **Preservation risks to monitor:** (a) the **statutory sunset of September 30, 2030** absent reauthorization; (b) ICR expiration Aug. 31, 2027; (c) the fact that the longest-run data (1947–2005) exists mainly as database tables and scanned-era publications rather than APIs; (d) general federal budget pressure on economic statistics programs.

---

## 8. Verification of the User's Description — Corrections and Refinements

Your description is accurate in substance. Three refinements:

1. **Sector naming:** The official description is "professional, **scientific**, and technical services (except legal)" (NAICS 541 excluding 5411), per Census's Federal Register notices; "professional and technical services" is a slightly truncated version.
2. **"Several U.S. Census Bureau reports... are produced using these data":** "Corporate Profits," "Retail Trade," and "Manufacturing, Mining, and Wholesale Trade" are actually the **QFR program's own press-release/publication titles** (issued quarterly by the QFR program itself), not separate Census programs consuming QFR data. The most important *external* consumer is the **BEA**, whose Corporate Profits estimates (NIPA table 6.16) and GDP/GDI rely on QFR — and the **Federal Reserve's Z.1 Financial Accounts**.
3. **"Currently collects...":** Accurate as of the latest Federal Register notice (Jan. 2024), which confirms the six-sector scope and 1947 origin. Note also that the asset thresholds differ by sector ($5M+ manufacturing per the current methodology document; $50M+ for other sectors, with historical $250K manufacturing language still appearing on some Census overview pages — worth citing the methodology PDF as the authoritative source).

---

## 9. Public Benefits — Summary for Policy Audiences

- **Measures the economy:** Without QFR, BEA's quarterly corporate profits estimates — a component of Gross Domestic Income used to gauge corporate-sector health, profit margins, and the "profit-led vs. wage-led" composition of national income — would lose their most timely industry-level input for roughly a third of corporate profits.
- **Monetary and fiscal policy:** Fed (Z.1, industry liquidity/leverage analysis), Treasury (tax-revenue forecasting), CEA, and Congress all rely on it.
- **Market transparency:** Provides the only free, public, quarterly, industry-and-asset-size-classified financial statements of private (non-public) U.S. corporations — SEC filings cover only listed firms, and IRS/SOI data arrive with multi-year lags.
- **Benchmarking:** Enables small and mid-sized firms, trade associations, lenders, and analysts to benchmark profitability, debt structure, and liquidity against industry peers.
- **Efficient design:** A rotating-panel mandatory sample of ~10,000 firms achieving national economic statistics for ~83,000 annual respondent-hours — a frequently cited example of statistical program efficiency (House Report 114-237 explicitly documents Congress's assessment of the program's value in reauthorizing it through 2030).

---

**Assessment date:** October 2026. This assessment draws on the Census Bureau's QFR program pages, the 2025–2026 economic indicator release calendars, the QFR methodology document, OMB/reginfo ICR records, the American Statistical Association's "The Nation's Data at Risk" report, Reuters/AP/NPR/Federal News Network coverage, and the Census Director's August 2026 disclosure-avoidance blog.

**Key context discovered:** The single most important QFR-specific development since January 2025 is **Department of Commerce Administrative Order (DAO) 216-26, "Disclosure Avoidance for Statistical Products"** (signed by the Secretary, effective June 4, 2026). QFR is the *only* principal economic indicator the Census Bureau has publicly identified as affected: between 2023Q4 and 2026Q1 QFR used "noise injection" to perturb published cell values; **beginning with the September 8, 2026 (2026Q2) release, QFR switched to cell suppression** in compliance with the order. Meanwhile, the Census Bureau as a whole has experienced severe staffing and leadership disruption, and the October–November 2025 shutdown suspended several other Census economic indicators — but QFR releases have stayed on schedule throughout.

---

## 1. Historical Data Availability

**Evidence for No Known Issue:**
- The QFR historical data pages remain fully populated and live: historical press releases for every quarter of 2024 and 2025 (and earlier years through 2009 for releases), historical publications from 1996–present, Excel publication tables from 2006–present, and the historical database tables spanning 1947–present (census.gov/econ/qfr/historic.html; census.gov/econ/qfr/mmws/hist_releases.html; hist_publications.html — all verified live as of this assessment).
- The interactive time-series tool (census.gov/econ/currentdata?programCode=QFR) and the Census Data API (timeseries/eits/qfr) remain operational.
- No reports, news coverage, or program-page notices indicate that any pre-2026 QFR file has been removed, altered, or taken offline. Notably, the noise-injected vintages (2023Q4–2026Q1) were published with full documentation of the distortion introduced, and remain posted.

**Evidence for higher levels:** None found. Broader reporting (Federal News Network, Dec. 2025, "'Bedrock' federal data sets are disappearing") documents removals elsewhere in the statistical system, but nothing QFR-specific.

**Finding: No Known Issue.** All historical vintages, including the full 1947–present database series, remain publicly accessible with no known alterations.

---

## 2. Future Data Availability

**Evidence for No Known Issue:**
- Every QFR release has occurred on schedule through 2025–2026: Q1 2025 (June 10, 2025), Q2 2025 (Sept. 9, 2025), Q3 2025 (Dec. 15, 2025), Q4 2025 (March 23, 2026), Q1 2026 (June 8, 2026), Q2 2026 (Sept. 8, 2026). The Q3 2026 release is scheduled for Dec. 7, 2026 (2025 and 2026 Economic Indicator Release Calendars; QFR release schedule page).
- Critically, QFR was **not** among the indicators suspended during the record 43-day government shutdown (Oct. 1–Nov. 12, 2025), even as the Advance Economic Indicators Report, Advance Services Report, and Preliminary Steel Products reports were marked "Suspended" on the Census calendar. The Q3 2025 QFR release came out on time on Dec. 15, 2025, immediately after the shutdown ended.
- The ICR (OMB Control No. 0607-0432) remains active; the current clearance (approved Aug. 15, 2024) does not expire until Aug. 31, 2027 — roughly a year away, consistent with the program's routine three-year renewal cycle (five consecutive renewals since 1990).

**Evidence for Moderate Risk:**
- The ICR expires in under a year (Aug. 31, 2027); a lapse or delayed renewal would trigger Moderate under the rubric. No 2026 renewal submission was identifiable in my research, though renewals are normally filed 6–12 months ahead.
- DAO 216-26 adds a mandatory individualized legal review of each statistical product before release, which the Data Foundation and Brookings warn could affect release timing for high-frequency indicators.

**Finding: No Known Issue.** Publication has met every statutory and scheduled deadline through the most recent release (Sept. 8, 2026), the ICR is active, and the program survived a once-in-a-generation shutdown without interruption. The 2027 ICR expiration and the new legal-review step are watch items, not current failures.

---

## 3. Data Quality

**Evidence for High Risk:**
- Effective with the 2026Q2 release (Sept. 8, 2026), QFR switched from noise injection to **cell suppression** per DAO 216-26. Suppression withholds cell values (shown as "D") rather than publishing every cell with small perturbations, so detailed industry × asset-size tables from 2026Q2 forward will likely contain fewer published cells than the 2023Q4–2026Q1 vintages.
- The DAO's per-product legal review requirement introduces a new potential source of release delay.

**Evidence for Moderate Risk:**
- The change is a **reversion**, not a novel degradation: QFR used suppression for decades before adopting noise injection in 2023Q4 (QFR Methodology, "Between reference quarters 2023Q4 and 2026Q1, QFR used... Noise Injection"). Relative to the dataset's long-term baseline, granularity is unchanged, and accuracy arguably *improves* (published values are no longer perturbed by injected noise).
- Frequency (quarterly) and timeliness (~75/90-day release lags) are unchanged. Sector coverage, sample design, and asset-size detail all remain intact.

**Finding: Moderate Risk.** The disclosure-avoidance switch is a real, administration-driven change to how QFR data are published, and it creates genuine uncertainty about cell-level availability in detailed tables going forward — but only one release (2026Q2) has occurred under the new regime, its net effect on published detail relative to the historical norm is unclear, and timeliness and frequency have been maintained. This is best characterized as an emerging risk to granularity rather than a demonstrated reduction.

---

## 4. Statutory Context

**Evidence for No Known Issue:**
- QFR is one of the most explicitly mandated federal statistics: **13 U.S.C. § 91 directs that "The Secretary shall collect and publish quarterly financial statistics of business operations... including data on sales, expenses, profits, assets, liabilities, stockholders' equity"** — the statute names exactly what must be collected and that publication must be quarterly. Response is mandatory (13 U.S.C. § 224).
- QFR is required for implementation of a core federal program: it is BEA's primary source for quarterly corporate profits estimates in the National Income and Product Accounts/GDP, and source data for the Federal Reserve's Z.1 Financial Accounts and Treasury tax forecasting.
- No genuine substitute exists: IRS SOI corporate data arrive with roughly a two-year lag, lack quarterly frequency and asset-size detail; SEC data cover only publicly listed firms, while QFR covers private corporations. Congress has affirmatively assessed the program's value five times, most recently reauthorizing it through Sept. 30, 2030 (P.L. 114-72, H. Rept. 114-237).

**Evidence for Moderate Risk:**
- The authorization carries a **sunset date of Sept. 30, 2030**, requiring future congressional action — but reauthorization has been routine and non-controversial for four decades.

**Finding: No Known Issue.** The statutory mandate is explicit and specific, the program has irreplaceable federal-program uses, and no alternative collection can substitute.

---

## 5. Staffing and Funding

**Evidence for High Risk:**
- **Staff losses exceed the 1,000-employee threshold:** the Census Bureau lost an estimated **15% of its staff since FY2024** (ASA, "The Nation's Data at Risk"); AFGE reports **1,300–1,500 employees** departed via the deferred resignation program alone, plus ~100 reduction-in-force notices at the Tucson call center during the October 2025 shutdown (Bloomberg Law; GovExec; The Census Project).
- **Leadership removed:** Senate-confirmed Director Robert Santos resigned in February 2025; Deputy Director Ron Jarmin served as acting director until September 2025, when **George Cook, a Commerce political appointee, was installed as acting director** (ASA report; NPR).
- Multiple division/office chiefs departed (NPR, April 2025); a Commerce IG evaluation found the Bureau lacks strategies to address staffing gaps; the hiring freeze and a 3,000+ item contract-approval backlog further strained operations.
- FY26 budget request cut current-survey staffing ~2% and periodic-census staffing 27%; ASA warned the trend "may mean the end of some specialty surveys."

**Evidence for a lower level:**
- Overall Census funding has not been cut 20%; the FY26 request kept total FTEs roughly flat (8,408→8,637, driven by reimbursable work), and economic-indicator programs appear to have been prioritized (QFR releases stayed on schedule through the disruption).

**Finding: High Risk.** The 1,000+ staff-loss threshold and the leadership change are each independently sufficient under the rubric, and both have occurred. QFR-specific staffing is not publicly broken out, but it sits within an agency that has lost ~15% of its workforce and its confirmed leadership.

---

## 6. Policy

**Evidence for High Risk:**
- **DAO 216-26 is an administration-driven directive that specifically changes QFR**: the Census Director's own blog names QFR as the affected economic indicator — "The Quarterly Financial Report is affected and will switch back to suppression" — and the QFR website now carries a standing policy note that all releases from Sept. 8, 2026 forward implement disclosure avoidance per the order. This is a significant change to what is published, made in accordance with Administration priorities, and already in effect rather than merely proposed.
- Analysts (Brookings, Data Foundation, APDU) warn the order's coarsening/suppression hierarchy and mandatory per-release legal review could reduce data detail and delay releases for affected products.
- The surrounding policy environment is hostile to statistical capacity: the 43-day shutdown forced suspension/cancellation of several sibling Census indicators (Advance Economic Indicators Report, Advance Services Report, Steel Products), Reuters reported Census "implementing strategies to bring economic data releases back on track" (Dec. 2025), and other Census surveys/tests were cancelled in 2025 (NPR).

**Evidence for Moderate Risk:**
- The QFR-specific change is methodologically two-sided: it removes the noise distortion that perturbed published values from 2023Q4–2026Q1, which proponents (including Census leadership) frame as improving accuracy and trust. It is not a content, topic, or scope change — sector coverage, items collected, and frequency are untouched.
- No QFR content has been altered for ideological reasons (e.g., no DEI- or terminology-driven changes, which have affected other datasets elsewhere in government).

**Finding: High Risk.** The determining fact is that a Commerce Department order issued under the current Administration has already, as of September 2026, changed how QFR data are published (suppression replacing noise injection, plus a new pre-release legal review) — squarely matching the rubric's "other significant changes in accordance with Administration priorities." The mitigating consideration (possible accuracy improvement) affects how severe the change is, not whether one has occurred.

---

## Summary of Risk Levels

**Historical Data Availability: No Known Issue**
All historical QFR files — publications (1996–present), Excel tables (2006–present), press releases, and the 1947–present database series — remain fully accessible with no known alterations.

**Future Data Availability: No Known Issue**
Every release through Q2 2026 (Sept. 8, 2026) has been on schedule, including through the record 43-day government shutdown that suspended sibling indicators; the ICR is active until Aug. 31, 2027. Watch items: ICR renewal and DAO-driven legal-review delays.

**Data Quality: Moderate Risk**
The DAO 216-26 switch from noise injection to suppression (effective 2026Q2) creates an emerging, not-yet-quantified risk to cell-level granularity in detailed tables, though it reverts to the program's long-standing historical method and removes prior perturbation; frequency and timeliness are unchanged.

**Statutory Context: No Known Issue**
13 U.S.C. § 91 explicitly mandates quarterly collection and publication of precisely the data QFR produces; the program is essential to BEA's NIPA corporate profits estimates with no viable substitute; reauthorized through Sept. 30, 2030.

**Staffing and Funding: High Risk**
The Census Bureau has lost ~15% of staff since FY24 (1,300–1,500 via deferred resignation alone, exceeding the 1,000-staff threshold), plus ~100 shutdown RIFs; the confirmed Director resigned in Feb. 2025 and was replaced by a political appointee. Budget cuts are below the 20% threshold, but the staffing and leadership criteria independently trigger High Risk.

**Policy: High Risk**
Commerce DAO 216-26 (June 2026) is an administration-driven change that specifically alters QFR's publication methodology (suppression replacing noise injection, implemented with the Sept. 8, 2026 release, with a standing policy notice on the QFR site), amid a broader pattern of disruption to Census economic indicators (shutdown suspensions of sibling reports). The change's accuracy effects are debatable, but a significant administration-priority-driven change to the data product has demonstrably occurred.

**Overall characterization:** QFR is a resilient program — statutorily anchored, schedule-consistent through extraordinary disruption, and with its deep historical archive fully intact. Its principal risks are institutional (a depleted parent agency with unstable leadership) and methodological (an administration-ordered disclosure-avoidance regime whose long-run effect on published detail and release timeliness remains to be seen). Preservationists should be most concerned about the agency-level staffing/leadership situation and the possibility that suppression reduces cell availability in future detailed tables; there is no immediate threat to the historical record.
